data: Great game, beautiful visuals, great story, music and effects, 10/10 would recommend
Amazing soundtrack, amazing graphics, amazing gameplay
Graphics are amazing, world is amazing, sound is amazing, love the dark, ambiguous atmosphere
10/10 would recommend if you are looking for a challenging puzzle game
Bland puzzles and unsatisfying story, alternate ending isn't worth going for either
unfortunately the gameplay is not for me
I also find it disappointing that completing the main story earns no achievement, with all 14 achievements tied to hidden collectibles instead
the narrative excuses itself from any such responsibilities or having to supply internal worldbuilding coherence, dramatic payoff, or resolution to its totalitarian premise
For me, games should be enjoyable throughout the experience, not merely something to endure in anticipation of a potentially impressive ending
I just found the linear gameplay boring
Too many sections rely on precise timing, repetitive trial and error, and platforming mechanics rather than clever puzzle-solving
spent 30 minutes trying to get simple keyboard controls to work and gave up

This was my favorite indie title I have beaten so far. The ending was great, even though I wasn't really paying attention to the story until 2/3 of the game.

10/10 would fuse into a huge meat blob of children again.(Not IRL)

INSIDE is confusing. It doesn't give any context or explanation for what's going on in the game. Throughout, not a single word is uttered, not through a narrator, nor through conversation, nothing. The only thing you know is that you're a child in a dark, post apocalyptic world who is alone and being pursued. Your only goal is to live, which encourages you to try to figure out what's going on by your own assumptions. It's really great.

I cannot recommend this dark, very atmospheric puzzle platformer highly enough. Its definitely not for everyone - the tone is dark throughout and positively black in the third act. But if you liked Limbo you should definitely check it out. It's a beautiful work of dark, twisted, insane genius

10/10 would not recommend to my grandmother...

Creepy and atmospheric setting, with solid gameplay--as you progress through the game, you learn new things and get to apply that knowledge in new ways. For me, at least, there was never a time when I had learned something way too long ago, and to progress I had to suddenly remember that the flamzit would blong if you harpered it correctly. Instead, you were reminded to harper the flamzit throughout the game so when you needed someting blonged, it was never a mystery, and the game instead focused on showing you that if you harpered whelp instead of harpering wharp, you could blyn instead of blong, which would get you into the next section.

So to speak.

Maybe don't play the game if you're grossed out easily; there's a lot of disturbing imagery (more body horror-ish; less blood and gore).

About as perfect a game as a game is likely to get.

An absolute masterpiece, and a gift we are lucky to have.
Great game, marked the start of one true 2d horror, great storyline and the puzzles were just the right amount of challenge. Would definitely recommend.

The clever environmental puzzles please the mind, the incredibly detailed environment, art and story amaze the imagination and the senses, and the constant threat of danger around every corner is both engaging and incredibly rewarding when you avoid it on the first try, while not too punishing if you don't. This game is short, but every second is fun, thought provoking and memorable. If you've played limbo and thought it was a masterpiece of art and game design, this game surpasses it in all regards. Play it!

Very short but very good.
Simple gameplay but not boring and very smooth, especially the transitions when loading different segments.
Very atmospheric.
Good amount of creepy and unsettling.
Enjoyed being a big fleshy blob.

I recomend this game to anyone who loves solving problems. I especialy love how simple the controls are yet with few controls to learn the developer still manages to create puzzles that make you think. Another very good feature of this game is that it auto saves at every hard part so you don't loose progress. I found the puzzles increasingly difficult as expected as the game progressed until a point very near the end where it seems to have gotten easier. The game was so captivating that I only shut it down once for sleep and finished it the following day. I feel that if you pace yourself and not binge play it, that it would not feel short like it did for me. Mostly because I was enjoying myself so much and did not want it to end.
Dark, clever, carefully crafted platformer, that forces you to think not only about how to solve the puzzles, but also about what you see on the screen in general.

Excellent , excuisite atmosphere,art direction,lighting and sounds. Sublime attention to detail.
A rather lacking end and may not net you many gameplay hours but apart from that a superb game, well worth it. The only thing I dislike is how I need to wait for another 4-5 years to see the next game from Playdead!:)
From the creators of LIMBO, also a very cool and unsettling game. The puzzles are well made, the atmosphere is fitting and overall it’s a good experience (on sale it costs like 2 bucks)

Well what to say about this so called piece of "art"? Not much to be honest. The story is simple: you (the player who sits behind his monitor) are the one who is chasing the little kid and basically you are the main protagonist. Atleast that was my interpretation of it and that was clear for me after playing 10 minutes. So you chase this little kid for 4 hours through the game and in the end you get him stuck in a pile of human bodies and thats it.

I didnt enjoyed this game at all because it tries to be edgy and deep as f*ck but fails miserably. The "puzzles" are a joke because you dont even need 3 brain cells to beat it.

I'll bury this game "INSIDE" a rotten human corpse and it will never see the sunlight again. (Now that was edgy & deep.)

Fantastic platform puzzler that has an amazing atmosphere. Its so pleasing that your brain might even want to replay it. Playthrough was around 6 epic hours for me. so good.

ps. rebind your keys in the menu, easy.

As amazing as this game is, 20eur for 3h of gameplay (assuming you get stuck for a while on some of the puzzles, otherwise is just a couple of hours long), it's definitely not a fair price point. I loved the art, the sound, the level design (except for the middle section, with the multi-level puzzles), the ambient, the bits of storytelling, the puzzles... it's a great game no doubt. But it ends in a weirdly unsatisfying way and it's totally not worth the entry fee (even at half price, I would consider it a bit on the expensive side for the amount of gameplay you get out of it). I would rate this one 6/10 with a positive rating all things considered, but all the reviews seem to be positive so I wanted to provide a bit of a different point of view.

My full video review here - https://youtu.be/KaoaHVA2ucw

This game caused me a bit of anxiety playing it. Not the greatest when it comes to being chased.... but then again this is a 2D sidescroller? Why am I being anxious due to a sidescroller? Well Inside really draws you into its world from the get go. Playing alongside a young boy who isn't as physically impressive as the adults or hunting dogs chasing him down. Inside tells a weird and dark tale throughout its 3-4 hour experience and is worth every penny. For those into sharing theories, Id strongly recommend you pop online after completing the game and share your thoughts as the games story is open for interpretation and boy does it have a lot to offer!!

Playdead, crushed it with INSIDE. The amazing visuals paired with engaging puzzles and a crazy imaginative world, filled with controllable zombies, crazy science experiments, and the chick from The Ring. I haven't been that surprised or laughed that hard at a game... probably ever. An absolute favorite!
Great puzzle game! The calm music tells me that I am doing well throughout the level. I like it. I would recommend this game to anyone who wants to find clues and try to solve them.

This side-scroller is like playing a silent story. There's no dialogue or text and the game just throws you in and you just go. It plays a lot like Limbo and if you liked Limbo you'll love Inside. You play a boy exploring or possibly escaping what appears to be a science lab or shadow government secret where they're "playing God". The game doesn't tell you much but that's what's fun about it. The story is kind of subjective. This would make for an interesting conversation if two or more players who have played this talked about it over coffee. There's some parts of the game that's like a puzzle but not too difficult. There's also hidden orbs you can find but for the sake of spoilers I won't say more than that. It's an easy to play game and pretty short but very worth it.

Pros
Gameplay
Simplistic
Subjective storyline
Creative puzzles but not too hard to figure out.
Visuals
Easy to backtrack using load menu
Half puzzle, half running for your life
There's a secret ending

Neutral
Short - not a long game but appropriate for this title

Cons
The ending is bizarre which is ok but then...anticlimactic.

love this game and for 2$ during the steam sale, it was well worth it. amazing how some of the simplest game mechanics were able to stump me a couple times on what to do. highly recommend if the price is rite. the game will only take a few hours to beat it
Without a single spoken word, or written line of text, this game tells a bizarre story I loved playing through. Fantastic game!

One of the best graphics I've ever seen, probably the best fun graphics and it's always surprising you with dynamics. I played LIMBO and loved it but it was very short (yes, a note for the DEVs) and I hope that INSIDE lasts a little bit longer but so far so good. And just a suggetion: play it with your GF/BF.

Long story short:

Worths every penny.

Buy this game.

Before this game I played Limbo from the same studio. I definitely liked the tension and vibe it created - it was a good mix between fast chase elements and slow challenges. The puzzles were well thought out and weren't repetitive. Overall I would say it was well spent couple of hours. The only think I would add is some narration.

the production value and attention to detail in this game is incredible and the game controls well but...

i just don't get it?

on one end of the story spectrum is a story that spoonfeeds you all the details, but this game is on the complete opposite end. is the story literal? is it some metaphor? i don't know and frankly have no reason to care. the puzzles are unique but there are so few of them and they are all relatively easy to solve. there are so many other games with more interesting story and better puzzles (portal 2, talos principle to name a few).

it's short though, and everyone seems to like it so give it a play if you are interested.

One of the best games I've ever played. Made by the Creators of Limbo, you start off in the same weird-art styled forest. From there the journey is much more complex and different. A more clear story is told (even though it's still a loose story left up to interpretation) through the majority of the gameplay. The sick platformer puzzles and the depth in the detail and graphics make this game a masterpiece. I loved every second of this, and with the hidden secret ending makes this game that much better. Doing it without a review seems impossible or nearly close to it.
Regardless, 10/10 game. They took one of the most successful indie games and turned it into something even better than before.

A mysteriously dark game that throws you right into this depressing, monochromatic, and harsh world.

INSIDE keeps you on your toes as you escape the unknown to a destination that's even less known.

This game is entirely driven by physics and they absolutely NAIL every aspect of it. The interactions feel clean and polished and the animations are incredibly responsive to the world. Coming from someone who does not enjoy puzzle games, the challenges in this are rewarding, intuitive without sacrificing on difficulty.

A very short experience that's dystopian sci-fi story leaves you wondering what else is inside.

INSIDE is very much like LIMBO, but better in every way. The atmosphere, soundtrack, environments, and gameplay are all top-notch. If you liked LIMBO, you'll like INSIDE.

It can be beaten with all achievements and endings in less than 10 hours, and has no replayability value, so keep that in mind when debating whether to buy it full-price or on sale.

It starts with a very fluid scroller that gets you in the mood to protect that kid.
Then the environment gets darker and darker.
But why are you a kid ? Why are you running to what looks like a more and more dangerous place ?
What happened to the world ?
This game is a speechless naration where the only way to understand is to watch the carefuly designed world and imagine by yourself what all this is about.
It can be pretty violent and this contrasts with the cute kid you embody in a post apocaliptical world where seemingly very few humans survived.
It has a sweet dose of fright, stress and awe that makes you want to do it in one go. The puzzles are never that hard which helps in getting the flow of the untold story through the places you visit.

A game definitely worth the detour and experience despite its short duration.
great game. i am still unable to understand the story , final ending completely but it's a great experience.
This game is good. I really like the art style; it's just like Little Nightmares.

play limbo first
this game improves on every aspect of limbo except the difficulty which i found to be much easier in this game
its probably a 10/10 although very short so just play after you play limbo because they are both amazing
This game looks stunning. You are basically playing a piece of art. The puzzles are quite challenging and are super creative. It was fun to play.

Played it again with a friend just to see it all again. Every time I thought I knew where the game was going it proved me wrong, and I love that, even if it did end up leaving me with more questions than answers. This game is relatively short but is so intuitive, intriguing, cinematic, and gripping that it goes down as a must play in my book.

Inside is quite simply a brilliant work of art. I absolutely adore the minimalist color palette and the incredibly messed up story implied by little details in the background and foreground. It's filled to the brim with tension and enhanced by its ingenious sound design and an atmospheric musical score particularly noteworthy at specific points with a specific enemy. I have a great deal of admiration for games like Inside that strive for complete immersion instead of using obtrusive on-screen button commands or hand-holding tutorials. Not that on-screen button commands are always a bad thing, but it's refreshing to play a game that prefers giving contextual clues. The puzzles are clever and balanced in perfect Goldilocks fashion, not too hard, not too easy and are incredibly satisfying upon completion. It's a short, but extremely memorable, thought provoking, and haunting experience. More than worth a buy.

Overall it is a really fun game in an interesting way. The game constantly made me have to know what's at the end of this 3 hour thrill ride of a game. Starts sorta slow, but after 20 minutes you get a taste for whats in store. What impressed me the most was the smooth controls and physics. I wouldn't call this LIMBO 2, although if you like LIMBO I would highly recommend it. Get it on sale for less than 10 bucks if price worries you, but make sure you play it no matter what.

Graphics 8/10
Physics 10/10
Puzzles/Challenges 8/10
Story N/A
Overall 9/10
really good game, did need to look up a tutorial here and there but i may just be stupid so. would recommend if you love games like Little Nightmares and dystopian genres
Gameplay, atmosphere, and audio are great. Story is basically non-existent and like something only a child would think is deep and meaningful.
The further I progressed in the story the more questions I had. Extremely weird game but i enjoyed it. It left me confused as shit tho.

Very good game. Like Limbo. The atmosphere is incredible. Mystery, fear, curiosity. Very good dark graphisms and sounds are frightening. Puzzles become harder and harder. Just did not understand for the moment the benefits of finding "secret balls".

I played the predecessor to Inside (Limbo) in 2010 or so, and I love what the devs have done with this game in comparison. In Limbo, touching water would instantly make you drown, here they've not only implemented swimming but even give you a damn submarine. The puzzles are still the perfect balance between creative, difficult, and doable in a reasonable amount of time. The only thing I'd criticize is the excessive amount of running/walking you sometimes have to do. Though the game is really pretty to look at, after playing for 2+ hours the ambiance just by itself can get a bit repetitive/boring.

Amazing game. What it lacks in length, it makes up for in quality tenfold. Visuals, audio, design, and atmosphere are perfect. A majority of the gameplay is plaforming, with a fair amount of really well-made puzzles with interesting mechanics. The story is mostly subtle, and a lot of it is left up to player interpretation. If you're bad at picking up on context clues or reading the environment you probably won't get a lot of the story that's there - even if you are there's going to be a lot of mystery. I got the game on sale, but I think I'd be comfortable paying full price for it.

It's also worth noting that this doesn't suffer from any of the shortcomings LIMBO (Playdead's previous game) did - there's no trial and error and mechanics are introduced naturally and organically. The game is perfect, pick it up.
This game should be felt. I can't really use words to describe it, I wish I could upload my emotions instead. That would certainly be a better review.

Inside deserves all the praise that it received when it first came out. The game has a lot going for it. There is a story being told, but it's told in such an elaborate way that it makes one ponder. There are multiple ways to look at each give situation because the story is told through the visal aspects instead of text or video form. It's one of the best games I have played because truly is a unique experience that will leave you thinking for hours after completing it. I highly recommend this game, and encourage others to give this game a shot. It's amazing.

Compared to Little Nightmares, this one is more puzzle based than stealth based. It's different enough in that respect where both Inside and Little Nightmares can be enjoyed, even though Little Nightmares is obviously heavily inspired by Inside.

This is a masterpiece and every single scene is beautiful. It's so smooth it looks like a painting. It's got a very interesting and fucked up narrative, superb sound design, responsive controls, and it's all backed up by perfect technical execution. Small but perfectly formed.
seems like a cool game, i wouldn't know. spent 30 minutes trying to get simple keyboard controls to work and gave up. Don't waste your time. I guess this thing is too old.
amazing puzzle game with really eerie atmosphere. fairly short(for me it was 5 hours) but still extremely memorable, but maybe wait for a discount before buying.

Took just over 4 hours to "complete" the game (did not get all achievements) and it was really good. Awesome visuals and sound and the story was quite interesting and unexpected.

Really good, would recommend. Similar to Little Nightmares.
this game is beautiful this is the best game i have ever played the story the game play truly a masterpiece oh and i beat the game

I loved Limbo and I love trailers that tell you zero about what the game is actually about. Saw that it's mechanically similar to Limbo and aesthetically like a ‘80s B-movie horror. I told myself can't wait to buy this. I was not wrong. Masterpiece.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players often praise the story and characters, and the graphics and art too.
The main complaints focus on the story and on gameplay that some find linear and boring.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about gameplay more often than before, at 9% against 6% across all time.
Recent reviews point out that "completing the main story earns no achievement", so the full achievement list depends on hidden collectibles.
